### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **12** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-datasource`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, `@objectstack/service-storage`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **99** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**45** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0fb55fc2fca5590a76c1827d95bf7d1bacf22d02`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `enforceAuth (23 routes)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **160** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0fb55fc2fca5590a76c1827d95bf7d1bacf22d02` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `63ba9b300dd308d33bda76ce324082cf1058ac62` — the merge of head `3c2b4152f9693935ac039d2daeb3be8c83be74de` into base `0fb55fc2fca5590a76c1827d95bf7d1bacf22d02`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 63ba9b300dd308d33bda76ce324082cf1058ac62 && git checkout 63ba9b300dd308d33bda76ce324082cf1058ac62
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0fb55fc2fca5590a76c1827d95bf7d1bacf22d02 3c2b4152f9693935ac039d2daeb3be8c83be74de && git checkout -B drift-repro 0fb55fc2fca5590a76c1827d95bf7d1bacf22d02 && git merge --no-ff 3c2b4152f9693935ac039d2daeb3be8c83be74de

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0fb55fc2fca5590a76c1827d95bf7d1bacf22d02
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0fb55fc2fca5590a76c1827d95bf7d1bacf22d02` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3c2b4152f9693935ac039d2daeb3be8c83be74de`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #23367 body; ruling `6159880505`; claims `6173499602` and `6173194763` (the latter by the re-scoped claim's reference, file list only); the amendment `6178205488` (its three-path file list only); dev reports `6178148974` and `6179873073`; PR #23541 body, metadata and 81-file list; the three-dot net diff `origin/main...3c2b4152f9` (merge-base `989aa483fd`; its 81-path list is byte-identical to the PR's, +2741/−178); every touched source, test, generated and docs file at the head and at `origin/main`, with the untouched context around each hunk (`api-key.ts`, `resolve-authz-context.ts`, `auth-service.ts`, `error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, `auth-manager.ts`, `auth-plugin.ts`, `keys.ts`, `http-dispatcher.ts`, `settings-routes.ts`, `settings-service-plugin.ts`, `settings-service.ts` `set`/`setMany`, `storage-routes.ts`, `storage-service-plugin.ts`, `auth.manifest.ts`, `rest-server.ts`, `mcp/src/plugin.ts`, `admin-routes.ts`, `sharing-plugin.ts`, `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`, `resolve-execution-context.ts`, `sys-api-key.object.ts`, the seven translation files, the changeset, `error-catalog.mdx`, `connect-mcp.mdx`, `api/index.mdx`, the two reference pages, `api-surface/contracts.json`, `export-origins/contracts.json`, `engine-double-contract.pinned.json`); the new pins (`core/security/api-key-lifecycle.test.ts`, `runtime/src/api-key-lifecycle.pin.test.ts`, `rest-api-key-lifecycle.pin.test.ts`, `settings-routes.api-key-lifecycle.pin.test.ts`, `storage-routes.api-key-lifecycle.pin.test.ts`, `api-key-lifecycle.dogfood.test.ts`, the `auth-plugin.test.ts` block) and every fixture diff; the repo's `ql.update` precedent, `resolveServiceOrLoud`, `deriveWireFace`, `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` (the disposition vocabulary), `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (launch-window), the `Clause-②` recognisers, the `.changeset/23287-*` and `.changeset/23455-*` precedents on `origin/main`, the `OS_CLOUD_API_KEY` read sites; the head's 48 check-runs, read last.
Not read: any comment titled `## 席位核对`, `Collected`, the amendment's reasoning beyond its file list, any seat ACCEPT/pointer line, every other comment on the card and the PR, cloud and objectui checkouts (none in this container).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Ruling fidelity (items 1–4): right**, with one located nuance on the reminder.
   - *Key store stays `sys_api_key`*: right. The seam still looks up `sys_api_key` by hash alone (`packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts:677-681`); no dependency, table or package is added; the object changes only `last_used_at`'s description (`packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-api-key.object.ts:267-279`).
   - *Policy as auth configuration, defaults 90 / 365 / 90, 1-year grace from the landing*: right. Four `auth` keys with those defaults (`packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/auth.manifest.ts:370-418`); `AuthManager.resolveApiKeyLifecyclePolicy()` falls back to `API_KEY_DEFAULT_EXPIRY_DAYS`/`API_KEY_MAX_EXPIRY_DAYS`/`API_KEY_INACTIVITY_DAYS` = 90/365/90 (`auth-manager.ts:8229-8247`, constants at `api-key.ts:154-160`); `bindAuthSettings` binds the keys (`auth-plugin.ts:1914-1938`); the grace is `API_KEY_LEGACY_GRACE_DAYS = 365` from `startedAt` (`api-key.ts:170`, `legacyGraceEndMs` at `:338-341`), the landing recorded once at `kernel:bootstrapped` (`auth-plugin.ts:856-858`, `recordApiKeyPolicyStart` at `:1681-1711`).
   - *Longer `expires_at` refused at a located spot*: right. `keys.ts:206-222` answers `400 API_KEY_EXPIRY_TOO_LONG` naming the latest date; this is the only writer of `expires_at` a caller reaches (`handleKeysRequest` is POST-only, `keys.ts:111`; the data-API update whitelist on `sys_api_key` is `revoked` alone and `expires_at` is `readonly`, `sys-api-key.object.ts:34-36, 263, 368-372`).
   - *Inactivity by `last_used_at`, located code, not revoked*: right. `idleWindowStartMs` reads `last_used_at` (`api-key.ts:355-368`); `lifecycleRefusalOf` answers `API_KEY_INACTIVE` naming the date and "It is not revoked" (`:272-283`); the `lifecycle` return at `:716-717` precedes `stampAdmittedKey` at `:838`, so a refusal writes nothing (pinned: core test "a key idle more than 90 days is refused although this call would have stamped it", `updates` stays `[]`).
   - *Reminder ahead of the grace — keys page and 403 body*: right as far as this repo reaches. The 403 body names the date (`API_KEY_EXPIRED` message "…its one-year grace … ended on ${at}", `api-key.ts:250-262`; carried verbatim by REST at `rest-server.ts:2457-2461` and by every relaying door). The keys page is objectui's (claim `6173194763`: "No objectui change: the keys page's reminder copy is a consumer card"); this repo's half is the grace stamped onto `expires_at` at first admission (`api-key.ts:409-412`), a column every `sys_api_key` list view already shows (`sys-api-key.object.ts:131, 143, 155`). Nuance: a pre-policy key never admitted after the landing carries no stamped date, but such a key is refused `API_KEY_INACTIVE` at 90 days naming the landing (or, with inactivity off, `API_KEY_EXPIRED` naming the grace end), so no key reaches the grace end unstamped without being told the date in its 403.
   - *Distinct, located codes*: right. `API_KEY_EXPIRED` / `API_KEY_INACTIVE` / `API_KEY_REVOKED` registered under `@objectstack/core` (`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts:933-944`), `API_KEY_EXPIRY_TOO_LONG` under `@objectstack/runtime` (`:305-311`); each stamped through its declared wire pair (`api-key.ts:208-210`; `keys.ts:66`); catalog entries (`content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx:84-88, 437-452`).
   - *Docs name rotation*: right. `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx:129-176` "Key lifetime, inactivity and rotation" with the no-gap rotation sentence; `content/docs/api/index.mdx:72-76` points to it; cloud's agent-connection page is cloud's (the ruling's own pointer on cloud#2868).
   - *Item 4 (`OS_CLOUD_API_KEY` read first)*: right. It is the runtime's outbound bearer (`packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts:166`, `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:1214`) and the CLI publish token fallback (`packages/cli/src/commands/package/publish.ts:308`); never read by `resolveApiKeyAdmission`; the PR body names it untouched and marks cloud's own verification NOT MEASURED.
   - Nothing the ruling asks of this repository is missing. Outside it, by the ruling's own execution plan: the keys-page copy (objectui) and cloud's docs/reminder copy (cloud#2868).

2. **Seat decisions 1–5 and the two accepted deviations: right.**
   - (1) one PR — `Fixes #23367`, head `3c2b4152f9`. (2) the policy is auth configuration bound by `bindAuthSettings`, read through `IAuthService.resolveApiKeyLifecyclePolicy` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.ts:213-227`), and `ResolveAuthzInput.apiKeyLifecycle` is a REQUIRED (non-optional) key beside `userAuthGates` (`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts:210-224`), as is the sixth parameter of `resolveApiKeyAdmission`/`resolveApiKeyPrincipal` (`api-key.ts:654-666, 609`); all ten builders pass `apiKeyLifecyclePolicySourceOf(authService)` or an explicit `undefined` (`rest-server.ts:3289-3290`; `resolve-execution-context.ts:255-259`; `mcp/src/plugin.ts:259`; `sharing-plugin.ts:974-975`; `settings-service-plugin.ts:334-335`; `storage-service-plugin.ts:1242-1246, 1419-1420`; `admin-routes.ts:510-511`; `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:3372-3373`; `exec-context-seam.testkit.ts:131`; `qa/dogfood/test/armed.ts:222-223`). (3) the stamp is throttled and the inactivity verdict reads the pre-stamp row: `lifecycleRefusalOf(row, …)` at `api-key.ts:716` runs on the row as found, `stampAdmittedKey` at `:838` runs only after the verdict, the posture refusals and the gate computation — the test "inactivity reads the PRE-stamp value" pins both halves. (4) the anchor is `auth.api_key_policy_started_at`, never the process start: the manager's `startedAt` is only ever `this.config.apiKeyPolicyStartedAt` (`auth-manager.ts:8234-8237`), set only from the stored setting (`auth-plugin.ts:1933-1937`). (5) distinct codes, `EXPIRED_TOKEN` judged and not reused (ledger comment `:936-939`), the branded `ApiKeyLifecycleRefusalError` (`api-key.ts:213-238`), each face re-raises by brand, and a missed face fails closed (runtime pin: an unbranded throw spelling `API_KEY_REVOKED`/403 is still `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`).
   - Deviation A — NULL `last_used_at` counts from max(landing, `created_at`): implemented at `api-key.ts:361-367` (`createdMs > startedMs ? signing : landing`), pinned both ways ("counts from the landing, never from an EARLIER created_at"; "counts from the signing when the key was signed after the landing"); with no landing recorded, no inactivity is judged (`:362`, pinned).
   - Deviation B — the legacy grace is the constant `API_KEY_LEGACY_GRACE_DAYS = 365`, not a fifth setting: `api-key.ts:170`, exported (`core/src/security/index.ts:132`), pinned ("is stamped onto expires_at (landing + 365 days)"; "after the grace the key is refused API_KEY_EXPIRED, naming the date").

3. **Published contract surfaces and semver: right on every item but one sub-arm, which is a non-blocking note.**
   - `IAuthService.resolveApiKeyLifecyclePolicy?()` (optional, additive) and `ApiKeyLifecyclePolicy` (`auth-service.ts:62-87, 213-227`); `api-surface/contracts.json` and `export-origins/contracts.json` each gain exactly that one line in sorted position.
   - The four ledger codes are in `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` and in the regenerated reference pages (`contract.mdx` `+327 → +331`; four sorted bullets in both).
   - The new `@objectstack/core` exports (`core/src/security/index.ts:128-144`): five day/interval constants, three code constants, the status, `apiKeyLifecyclePolicySourceOf`, `ApiKeyLifecycleRefusalError`, `isApiKeyLifecycleRefusalError`, three types.
   - The four `auth` settings keys (`auth.manifest.ts:370-418`), translated in three locales.
   - `Clause-②: yes` is truthful (the published accept set widens: a contract member, four codes, exports, four settings keys); the changeset's arm `yes (narrowing)` is right — the key doors narrow, so it is BREAKING, carries the **BREAKING** banner and a `!` title, and ships as `minor` under the launch-window convention (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs:5`), the same shape as `.changeset/23287-api-key-account-posture.md:16-20`. Every package with a published source change is bumped `minor`: spec, core, runtime, rest, mcp, plugin-auth, plugin-sharing, service-settings, service-storage, service-datasource, cloud-connection, platform-objects (plugin-security and cli change tests only; qa/dogfood is a test package).
   - ADR-0087: the `not-required` half is right (no authorable key, stored shape or metadata surface moves; `sys_api_key` gains no column). The chosen sub-arm `(no-migration-prescription)` is the weaker of two honest arms: the changeset's last bullet is a host-code rewrite instruction ("Hosts calling `resolveAuthzContext` … pass `apiKeyLifecycle: …`, or the sixth argument"), which the gate's own definition of that arm names a self-contradiction that passes only on a detector miss (`scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs:147-153`, and its #8277/#18745 commentary); the precedent for the identical required-input narrowing, `.changeset/23455-key-admission-posture-required.md:13`, used `not-required (runtime-interface-only packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts#ResolveAuthzInput)`. The gate passes at this head (`Lint & Repo Gates` success) and both arms are `not-required`, so nothing lands wrong — see Acceptance notes.

4. **Refusal semantics at every face: right.**
   - REST: `computeExecCtx`'s catch keeps the brand beside the request and resolves no context (`rest-server.ts:3467-3475`), so every door keeps its fail-closed answer; `enforceAuth` answers `403 { error: { code, message } }` (`:2457-2461`) — the envelope the ADR-0069 gate refusal already uses at that door (`:2443`); an unknown key is `ANONYMOUS_DENY_BODY` 401; an unbranded throw goes to `rethrowAuthzStoreUnavailable` (503) or no context (401). Pinned (`rest-api-key-lifecycle.pin.test.ts:113-143`).
   - MCP stdio: per call the brand leaves `resolvePrincipal` as the thrown envelope (`mcp/src/plugin.ts:689-697`); at start it refuses to start naming the code (`:525-532`).
   - Datasource admin (`admin-routes.ts:528-532`), share links (`sharing-plugin.ts:996-1000`), install-local (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:3399-3403`): re-raised by brand beside the outage re-raise; every other throw keeps today's arm.
   - Runtime dispatcher, MCP HTTP included: the identity-step catch re-raises by brand ahead of `rethrowAuthzStoreUnavailable` (`http-dispatcher.ts:721`); pinned on the wire through the mounted `POST /api/v1/mcp` (`403 API_KEY_REVOKED` in an `ApiErrorSchema`-valid envelope, `403 API_KEY_INACTIVE`), the unbranded lookalike still 401, an unknown key 401, nothing inserted (`runtime/src/api-key-lifecycle.pin.test.ts:185-329`).
   - Settings: the resolver re-raises (`settings-service-plugin.ts:373`), the family door relays beside `relayAuthzStoreOutage` (`settings-routes.ts:165-169, 252-253`); pinned on every mounted route, unknown key 401.
   - Storage: `buildFileReadAuthorizer` re-raises (`storage-service-plugin.ts:1476-1481`); `authorizeDownload`'s catch relays (`storage-routes.ts:567-574`); unknown key `401 AUTH_REQUIRED`; nothing minted; pinned.
   - The dev's claim that `refuseHeldSession` is unreachable for the brand: right. Its reader `buildAuthGateSessionReader` calls `resolveApiKeyAdmission` directly (`storage-service-plugin.ts:1237-1249`), which returns the `lifecycle` outcome and can throw only `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` (`api-key.ts:705-713, 829`); the reader answers `undefined` for every outcome but `held`/`none` (`:1248-1249`); `refuseHeldSession`'s catch relays the outage brand and rethrows anything else (`storage-routes.ts:655-663`); the upload routes read only `getSession(headers)` (`buildAuthSessionResolver`). The brand is first raised by `resolveAuthzContext` (`resolve-authz-context.ts:498-501`), which that reader never calls.
   - Nothing is minted on a refusal: the `lifecycle` return at `api-key.ts:717` precedes the stamp at `:838`; the dispatcher and storage pins assert no insert / no capability.

5. **Write-side safety of the read path: right; two non-blocking notes.**
   - The `last_used_at` stamp: `ql.update('sys_api_key', { id, ...patch }, { context: { isSystem: true } })` (`api-key.ts:429`) is the repo's engine-dispatch shape (`auth-manager.ts:8325` `mfa_required_at`, `:8853` `last_activity_at`) and the new pins route it through `assertEngineUpdateDispatch`. The throttle is DB-held — a write only when the column is empty or ≥ `API_KEY_LAST_USED_STAMP_INTERVAL_MS` old (`:404-408`) — so it is idempotent and multi-node safe (a race costs one duplicate write of a near-identical timestamp, as the PR says). Failure is caught, never rethrown, said once per engine through a `WeakSet` latch at `error` with the consequence and the fix (`:413-425`); pinned (one call writes; throttle; held key stamped; said once; the dogfood real-engine write). A caller can only cause the write for the key it holds, with platform-chosen values.
   - The grace stamp: `expires_at = landing + 365 d` only when the row has no readable `expires_at` (`:409-412`); once written the branch never re-fires. Not reversible by a caller: `expires_at` is outside the data-API update whitelist and `readonly` (`sys-api-key.object.ts:34-36, 263, 368-372`), and the keys door is POST-only. Moving `api_key_policy_started_at` moves the date only for unstamped keys, as the changeset states. Reversal for a stamped key needs a system-context write (the MFA-grace precedent).
   - The landing anchor: written at `kernel:bootstrapped` only when the stored value's `source` is `default` (`auth-plugin.ts:1695-1699`), never overwritten; the write goes through `setMany` (in-process `ctx = {}` is permitted — `assertPermitted` guards enforced HTTP callers), which emits a change event (`settings-service.ts:2215`) → `subscribe('auth')` re-runs `applySettings` (`auth-plugin.ts:2196-2198`) → `applyConfigPatch` sets `apiKeyPolicyStartedAt` (`auth-manager.ts:4362+`, `this.config = next`). The manifest `pattern` matches `toISOString()` output. No settings service → `warn` once; a failed write → `error` with the remedy (`:1687-1693, 1700-1708`). Note: the check-then-set has no CAS, so two nodes booting on an empty store at the same instant can both write; the two values differ by the boot skew and every node converges on the stored one through `subscribe` — harmless.

6. **Signing door: right.** No `expires_at` → `now + defaultExpiryDays` (`keys.ts:224-226`), echoed (`:368`); past `now + maxExpiryDays` (60 s skew forgiven) → `400 API_KEY_EXPIRY_TOO_LONG` naming the latest date, nothing stored (`:206-222`); exactly one year accepted (runtime pin: +365 d accepted, +366 d refused; dogfood: 90-day default and the 400). The default never outlives the ceiling (`auth-manager.ts:8241-8243`, pinned). No auth service → pre-policy signing; a registered-and-broken auth service → `AuthzStoreUnavailableError('api_key_policy')` (`:196-204`, pinned). Update path: none exists — `handleKeysRequest` accepts only POST (`keys.ts:111`), and the data API strips `expires_at` on `sys_api_key` (`sys-api-key.object.ts:368-372`), so the ceiling bounds the only writer of `expires_at` a caller reaches.

7. **Generated files and docs: right.** `api-surface/contracts.json` and `export-origins/contracts.json` each gain one line in sorted position in the shape `gen:api-surface` writes; the reference pages gain `+327 → +331` and four sorted bullets in the shape `gen:docs` writes; `check:generated` rides the required `TypeScript Type Check` job, success at this head. The `en.objects.generated.ts` help text equals the source description byte-for-byte (`sys-api-key.object.ts:276-277`); the zh-CN / ja-JP / es-ES hand translations say the same three things (recorded on use, at most once an hour, refused after the inactivity window — 90 days by default — until replaced). The three service-settings translations are accurate, and their rendering of the NULL-use anchor ("from its creation, or from the policy start when it is older") matches the code's max(landing, `created_at`). `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` gains one entry in file-sorted position. `content/docs/releases/**` is untouched. The catalog count 52 → 56 is consistent: `wireCodes` = (StandardErrorCode ∪ codes the catalog page publishes) minus door-translated codes (`scripts/check-error-status-conformance.mjs:2143-2176`), and the page gains exactly the four headings; the pin `error-catalog-docs.test.ts:122-126` sits in `Test Core (1/6)`, success at this head.

8. **Size and scope: right.** 2919 changed lines (+2741/−178, 81 files; the local three-dot diff against `origin/main` at merge-base `989aa483fd` lists the same 81 paths as the PR), under 3000.
